title: Assessability and boundary labels
description: Assessability records whether the supplied footage lets a human judge a claim ('the footage did not make this attribute assessable' vs a real verdict). Boundary labels record ground-truth event onset/offset and the tolerance used for boundary-error scoring. See RAZIEL_Master_Execution_Plan_v1.3.md §21.3, §17.4, §22.1(5).

overall.description: Whether the declared observation region can be judged at all. Unassessable regions can never become a clean negative; visible_none over an unassessable region is unobservable.

reasons.description: Why a region is (un)assessable. `missing_coverage` (absent expected observation ticks) forces unobservable/undetermined, never a clean negative.

per_attribute.description: Optional per-attribute assessability, e.g. bag colour assessable but bag contents not.

start_pts.description: Ground-truth onset in source PTS seconds.

end_pts.description: Ground-truth offset in source PTS seconds (>= start_pts).

tolerance_s.description: Human boundary tolerance; boundary-error metrics are reported against this.

source.description: Boundary truth is human-derived. Retriever/auto proposals may accelerate development but never define test-boundary truth (§21.5).
